clue.text: Prisoner having battle to get soup

parts.note: a con is a convict, slang for a prisoner
the Somme was a great First World War battle in France

explanation.surface: A convict is promised soup after fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear meat broth served as a starter is a classic French soup.

clue.text: Birds not following other birds

indicators.note: not means the letter for following is left out

parts.note: fowls are birds, especially poultry
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Some birds refuse to follow the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooting nocturnal raptors are a family of birds.

clue.text: Petitioner to take the place of one held inside

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the other piece

parts.note: to supplant is to take the place of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone pleading to replace a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who humbly begs or pleads is a petitioner.

clue.text: Soldier's keeping it up in service

indicators.note: the soldier's word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men; 's adds S

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A soldier keeps singing through a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning prayer in the Anglican church is a religious service.

clue.text: Smoothing over Wakefield doctor's bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another comes above it

parts.note: evening a surface is smoothing it
Dr Primrose is the Vicar of Wakefield in Oliver Goldsmith's novel

explanation.surface: A Wakefield physician smooths over a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a flower. The Vicar of Wakefield is an 18th-century novel whose clergyman is Dr Charles Primrose.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered plant opening at dusk is a bloomer, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Swallowing a bit of cereal without liquid is no fun

indicators.note: one word taking in another is described as swallowing it, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: something without liquid is dry
an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant such as wheat

explanation.surface: Eating dry cereal with no milk is a joyless breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition 'no fun'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and gloomy offers no enjoyment.

clue.text: Spoiling mother on becoming old

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A mother keeps spoiling her children as she grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing harm to something is spoiling it.

clue.text: This crew's supernumerary is drunk

parts.note: a rowing crew of this size plus one spare suggests the saying one over the --- for a drunk

explanation.surface: An extra rower turns up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'one over the eight' is a British saying for being tipsy, from eight pints as a sensible limit; an eight is also a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew numbers that many oarsmen, and one over that number means tipsy.

clue.text: Reports air is contaminated — here's the answer

definitions.text: Reports air is contaminated — here's the answer

indicators.note: contaminated letters are fouled up and so mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: News of polluted air comes with a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the device to breathe through is the answer to foul air.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing mask filters out polluted air for the wearer.

clue.text: Follow another car closely and burn to sneak in front

indicators.note: the word for sneak is placed in front of the word for burn

parts.note: to slip somewhere is to sneak
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A reckless driver tailgates and tries to sneak past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like a racing verb, as in burning rubber; it is the Scottish word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing drivers tuck into the low-pressure wake of the car ahead to save effort.

clue.text: Ahead of time, serving Americans marrow

indicators.note: the servicemen come ahead of, in front of, the letter for time

parts.note: GIs are American servicemen

explanation.surface: American troops arrive early with a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marrow' suggests the vegetable, but here it means the innermost essence of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow of an argument is its core or essential substance.

clue.text: Undress on top of stairs where the flight ends

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a landing is the level floor at the top of a flight of stairs
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: Someone takes their clothes off at the head of the staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' seems to mean a flight of stairs, matching the surface; it is an aeroplane journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touches down on a runway at the end of its journey.

clue.text: National support at disturbance is welcomed by political leader

indicators.note: the inner pieces are taken in, welcomed, by the leader's letters

parts.note: PM is Prime Minister
taken as written
a riot is a disturbance
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister hosts a rowdy rally of loyalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Love of and backing for one's own country is national loyalty.

clue.text: Before writing article, dip into long story

indicators.note: the word for dip is set down before the article is written

parts.note: to sag is to dip or droop
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author settles into a lengthy tale before drafting a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelandic epic or any long family chronicle is a lengthy narrative.

clue.text: Dark grey material used in the Artillery

definitions.meaning: a bronze alloy once used to cast cannon

explanation.surface: A drab-coloured fabric is issued to the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: The copper-tin alloy for casting cannon gave its name to a blue-grey shade.

clue.text: One who takes up duties, having cut out servant

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A new employee takes on tasks after removing a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes up duties' sounds like starting a job; duties are taxes, collected by this officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer collecting excise taxes gathers duties on goods.

clue.text: Cunning daily's way to deal with buzzers

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or cunning
a daily is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: A clever newspaper suggests how to handle insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzers' could be doorbells; here they are flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky strips trap flies, a method of dealing with buzzing insects.

clue.text: Publicity about to disconcert chatterbox

indicators.note: the letters for publicity are placed around the next piece

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
to rattle someone is to disconcert them

explanation.surface: A publicist sets out to unsettle a talkative person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who babbles endlessly is a talkative person.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue

explanation.surface: Something to put in the pet's bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the fluffy Chinese breed and slang for grub share this short word.

clue.text: Disrobed round lake and made a lot of noise

indicators.note: the word for disrobed goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: bared means stripped, disrobed

explanation.surface: A skinny-dipper by the lake made a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet or radio sounding loudly made a great noise.

clue.text: Fool with lots of money protecting politician as result of fear.

parts.note: a goose is a silly person

indicators.note: the money surrounds, and so protects, the politician

parts.note: piles of money means lots of it
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A rich idiot shields a nervous parliamentarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumps rise on the skin when someone is frightened or cold.

clue.text: Artistic work that's religious, in the main

indicators.note: the religious letters sit inside the word for the main

parts.note: the main is a literary term for the sea
pi is short for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A devotional painting of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown-toned drawing or photograph is a work of art.

clue.text: Present that shows blonde's femininity?

parts.note: a word for present that splits into the feminine pronoun plus the final letter that makes blond feminine

explanation.surface: A gift reveals a fair-haired woman's girlishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is the definition, as in 'in attendance'; the rest plays on the feminine pronoun and on the E that marks blonde as the feminine form of blond.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in attendance is present in this place.

clue.text: As result of leg injury, having flexible cover

definitions.meaning: walking unevenly because of a hurt leg
a book in soft binding, not stiff boards

explanation.surface: An injured reader carries a paperback.
explanation.definitionFit: An injured walker hobbles, and a floppy binding is also called this.

clue.text: Computer expert supporting correct use of language in speech

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: the word for correct use of language is heard spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: grammar is the rules of correct language

explanation.surface: A technician backs proper spoken English.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the unstressed ending of the word for correct language sounds just like the last syllable of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coder who writes software is an expert with computers.

clue.text: Spoil one married couple

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A single wedded partnership goes sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or weaken something is to spoil it.

clue.text: Expose to injury from explosion of new grenade

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh bomb going off could hurt someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone at risk of harm is to imperil them.
